rules: id is the code's own id wherever it is unique (fin_cells.js cell ids, valuationBox measure ids, financials.json measure ids), so readerNotes.lines and readerNotes.measures resolve. Where the same code id names two different things on the page, the id carries a prefix (stmt., margins., chart., headline.) and codeId gives the code's id.

default is the day-one switch: MAIN = in the box's main view, ON = only when the box is expanded, OFF = nowhere. Day one reproduces the page as it was on 2026-10-02, as amended by D93 (Market cap label, no working row). Not-built and dropped entries are always OFF.

appliesTo for valuation measures is never copied: it points at valuationBox.measures[].suppressedFor. Financials cell types are recorded from fin_cells.js measuresFor and checked against it by tests/metric-catalog.test.mjs.
computed: false = a reported line; true = computed by Mowgli from reported lines; a string = computed only in the case it names.
series lists the chart series the payload carries for the metric (annual, quarters, ttm); a phase-2 chart picker chooses among them.

box.peek lists, in order, the catalog ids the collapsed box draws from today. A peek draws only from items that are not OFF: an item that is OFF is skipped and the peek falls to the next MAIN item in that box; with none, the box has no peek (lead ruling 2026-10-02, consistent with D90 "OFF = nowhere"). The fall-through takes only items of kind number or item. An item that does not apply to the company type or has no data in the payload loses its peek slot instead of falling through (matches today, e.g. a bank's empty Valuation peek), and so does a substitute hidden because its primary is drawn (lead ruling 2026-10-02).

locked: true marks an entry the resolver must never switch OFF (the name and price, D90; the Financials box notes). Its state may move between MAIN and ON only where its entry says so; a settings file that sets it OFF is refused.
codeId, on every entry whose id differs from the code's own id, is the payload-relative path in the same syntax as payload (for example fin.annual.rows[id=revenue]).

Peek-only entries (peekOnly: true, form peek, group peek) are drawn only in the collapsed peek of their box and nowhere else; ON or MAIN keeps them in the peek, OFF removes them from it. They exist where a peek shows a figure nothing else in the box draws (Financials: peek.revenue, peek.revenueGrowthQ; lead ruling 2026-10-02, so day one matches today).

meta.purpose: D90 data switchboard: Adam's switches for the company page. What each metric is, where it comes from and its day-one default live in data/reference/metric-catalog.json; this file holds only what Adam changes. The resolver is public/lib/switchboard.mjs.
meta.shape: boxes.order lists the boxes in placement order; boxes.pins puts a box directly under another, in its column. metrics.<id> and byType.<type>.<id> may set state (MAIN, ON, OFF), form (one of the entry's forms), order (a number, within its box), spot ("hero" puts it in the headline strip under the logo) and spotOrder. Each field falls back from byType[type] to metrics to the catalog default. chart is reserved for phase 2.
meta.dayOne: Empty metrics and byType reproduce the page as it was on 2026-10-02 (checked against tests/fixtures/switchboard-day-one.json by tests/switchboard.test.mjs). The agent changes a switch only when Adam says so (D90).
